# Proxlane

> One endpoint in front of every scraping API. Routes requests across ScraperAPI, ScrapingBee,
> Scrapfly and Bright Data with automatic failover, per-request cost visibility and honest block
> detection. AGPL, self-hostable, bring your own provider keys.

Proxlane is a gateway, not a scraper. It makes one request and returns one response, and the
response headers say what happened: which providers were tried, which served, what it cost,
and whether a block page was detected.

The header to branch on is `X-Outcome-Class`. It has six values and never grows.
`X-Outcome` is more precise but gains members over time.

## Docs

- [FAQ](https://proxlane.dev/docs/faq): what it does, what it costs, what happens to your keys.
- [Scraper returns 403](https://proxlane.dev/symptoms/403-while-scraping): why does my scraper get 403
- [200 response with a captcha page](https://proxlane.dev/symptoms/200-captcha-body): scraper returns 200 but body is a captcha
- [Cloudflare challenge page in Playwright](https://proxlane.dev/symptoms/cloudflare-challenge-playwright): playwright still gets the cloudflare challenge page
- [DataDome block detection](https://proxlane.dev/symptoms/datadome-detection): how to detect a datadome block
- [Quickstart](https://proxlane.dev/docs/quickstart): Make your first request in about a minute.
- [Hosting](https://proxlane.dev/docs/hosting): Where the gateway runs well, where it runs badly, and why.
- [API reference](https://proxlane.dev/docs/api): Every endpoint, parameter and header the gateway implements.
- [Outcomes](https://proxlane.dev/docs/outcomes): What every result means, what it returns, and whether to retry.
- [How failover works](https://proxlane.dev/docs/failover): Chains, detection, cooldowns and deadlines.
- [Bring your own provider](https://proxlane.dev/docs/adapters): Add a provider Proxlane has never heard of, and it joins the chain.
- [Using Proxlane from an agent](https://proxlane.dev/docs/agents): How to give an AI agent a scraping tool that fails honestly.
- [Use cases](https://proxlane.dev/docs/use-cases): What Proxlane is good at, and what it is not for.
- [Changelog](https://proxlane.dev/docs/changelog): What changed, per package, newest first.

## Tools

- [Scraping API comparison](https://proxlane.dev/scraping-api-comparison): what ScraperAPI, ScrapingBee, Scrapfly and Bright Data each charge on top of their base rate for JS rendering, residential proxies and country targeting, from their own published rates. Compares multipliers, which are dimensionless; never compares base rates across billing units.
- [Block page detector](https://proxlane.dev/block-page-detector): paste a response body and see whether it is a block page, which rule fires, and what the gateway would do with it. Runs client-side; makes no request to any target.

## Other formats

- [Everything in one file](https://proxlane.dev/llms-full.txt): every page concatenated.
- Raw markdown per page: add `.md` to any docs URL, e.g. https://proxlane.dev/docs/api.md
- [OpenAPI 3.1 description](https://proxlane.dev/openapi.json): every endpoint, parameter, header and status code.

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/proxlane/proxlane): AGPL-3.0 for the gateway; Apache-2.0 for the adapter, detection and shared packages.
- [Self-hosting guide](https://github.com/proxlane/proxlane/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md): Compose, VPS, reverse proxies and known gaps.

## Notes

- There is no MCP server and no published SDK. Use the HTTP endpoint.
- Proxlane does not defeat anti-bot measures. It reports when a provider was blocked.
- Provider keys stay in the gateway's environment. Clients authenticate to the gateway.
